question: A 62-year-old man presents to the emergency room with an acute myocardial infarction. Twenty-four hours after admission to the cardiac intensive care unit, he develops oliguria. Laboratory tests show that his serum BUN is 59 mg/dL and his serum creatinine is 6.2 mg/dL. Renal biopsy reveals necrosis of the proximal tubules and thick ascending limb of Henle's loop. Which of the following would you most likely observe on a microscopic examination of this patient's urine?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acute myocardial infarction -> Decreased renal perfusion -> Acute kidney injury -> Oliguria -> Elevated BUN and creatinine levels -> Renal tubular necrosis -> Microscopic examination of urine: Muddy brown casts -> 95%
analysis: The patient's presentation with oliguria, elevated BUN and creatinine levels, along with renal biopsy findings of necrosis of the proximal tubules and thick ascending limb of Henle's loop, is indicative of acute tubular necrosis (ATN). In ATN, the urine microscopy typically shows muddy brown casts, which are composed of cellular debris and casts of tubular epithelial cells.
